description: Translate the user-facing entry-point docs (README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/INDEX.md, docs/EXTENSION-GUIDE.md, docs/e2e-report-2026-02-14.md, docs/releases/v1.0.0-beta.md, docs/releases/v1.1.0-beta.md, docs/releases/v1.2.0.md, scripts/lib/README.md) from English to Brazilian Portuguese. These are the most-read files; getting them right sets the tone for everything else. Mixed-language files (notably AGENTS.md, which is mostly Chinese with English bullet keywords) translate ONLY the English passages.
steps: Read each target file in full before editing it. The targets are: README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/INDEX.md, docs/EXTENSION-GUIDE.md, docs/e2e-report-2026-02-14.md, docs/releases/v1.0.0-beta.md, docs/releases/v1.1.0-beta.md, docs/releases/v1.2.0.md, scripts/lib/README.md.

For README.md: translate prose, all headings, list bullets, blockquotes, and table cells that are natural language. Preserve every fenced code block verbatim. Preserve all GitHub badges (`![Release](...)` etc), all links, all `[text](url)` URLs and image refs. Preserve `oh-my-kiro` (the product name), `oh-my-zsh`, `Kiro`, `Kiro CLI`, `Ralph Loop`, `OMK`, all hook script names like `block-secrets.sh`, `enforce-ralph-loop.sh`. Translate the section bodies to Portuguese, keeping technical acronyms (API, REST, MCP, LSP, IAM, JSON, YAML, GraphQL, DNS, CI, OAuth, AST, TDD, SDK), consecrated terms (deploy, commit, push, pull request, branch, merge, hook, gate, plan, review, lint, runtime, framework, pipeline, webhook, endpoint, token, payload, middleware, scratchpad, worktree, submodule, rebase). Keep emojis exactly as-is. Keep ASCII boxes (the 3-Layer Determinism diagram and Ralph Loop diagram) structurally identical, but translate the prose lines inside them. The Chinese inline blocks under '### How It Works' (e.g. `correction-detect.sh fires (中英文 30+ 纠正模式匹配)`) must be left untouched.

For AGENTS.md: this file is overwhelmingly Chinese. Per the translation rules, do NOT translate Chinese to Portuguese. Translate ONLY the English text fragments — primarily the section heading words like 'Identity', 'Roles', 'Principles', 'Workflow', 'Authority Matrix', 'Skill Routing', 'Skill 安装规则', 'Knowledge Retrieval', 'Self-Learning', 'Enforcement', and any English bullet-prefix words such as 'Evidence before claims', 'As code', 'TDD driven', 'No hallucination', 'Fail closed', 'Minimal context, single source of truth', 'End-to-end autonomy', 'Think like a top expert', 'Never skip anomalies', 'Recommend before asking', 'Socratic self-check', 'No hacky workarounds', 'Bold reform over timid patches', 'Compound interest engineering', and the table headers '场景/Skill/触发方式/加载方式'. Pure Chinese parenthetical explanations stay in Chinese. Keep all hook script paths and table content verbatim. Use Portuguese equivalents for the heading-level English words (e.g. 'Identity' → 'Identidade'; 'Roles' → 'Papéis'; 'Principles' → 'Princípios'; 'Workflow' → 'Workflow' — keep 'Workflow' as it is consecrated in PT-BR tech writing; 'Authority Matrix' → 'Matriz de Autoridade'; 'Skill Routing' → 'Roteamento de Skills'). Translate the bullet labels but keep the parenthetical Chinese verbatim, e.g. 'Evidence before claims（任何完成声明前必须有验证证据，enforced by stop hook）' becomes 'Evidence before claims（任何完成声明前必须有验证证据，enforced by stop hook）' (no change — the English label is kept as a consecrated principle name). For the Skill Routing table header row '场景 | Skill | 触发方式 | 加载方式' leave it unchanged. After editing, validate that the file still parses as Markdown (no broken table rows).

For docs/INDEX.md: this is a table of plan/design/release index entries. Translate the table HEADERS ('Date', 'Type', 'Title', 'Link') to Portuguese ('Data', 'Tipo', 'Título', 'Link'). Leave each ROW's title verbatim (those titles are document filenames in slug form; translating them would not match the actual filenames). Translate any narrative prose above/below the table.

For docs/EXTENSION-GUIDE.md: translate all prose, section headings ('Add a Skill', 'Add a Hook', 'Install a Community Skill' → 'Adicionar uma Skill', 'Adicionar um Hook', 'Instalar uma Skill da Comunidade' or similar). Preserve every fenced code block, every JSON example, every CLI command. Preserve `bash tools/...`, `python3 scripts/...` literals.
For docs/e2e-report-2026-02-14.md: translate prose narrative and headings. Preserve test command outputs, hook IDs, file paths.

For docs/releases/v1.0.0-beta.md, v1.1.0-beta.md, v1.2.0.md: translate the bullet text (Highlights, Breaking Changes, Bug Fixes, etc). Keep proper-noun feature names (`@do` Command, OpenViking Semantic Search, Ralph Loop, etc). Keep version strings, dates, and code blocks intact.
For scripts/lib/README.md: short file, translate all prose. Keep the boundary-rule diagram structurally intact.
After each file edit, run `git diff --stat <file>` to confirm only that file changed. Do not introduce trailing-whitespace differences on unrelated lines.

Run baseline-preserving verification: `bash tests/test-agents-template.sh 2>&1 | tail -1` (must match baseline), and grep test-anchored literals on AGENTS.md if any of its section headings are referenced anywhere (search `grep -rn 'Authority Matrix\|Skill Routing\|Identity' tests/ hooks/ scripts/ | head` to confirm no test depends on the AGENTS.md heading wording).

Commit: `git add README.md AGENTS.md docs/INDEX.md docs/EXTENSION-GUIDE.md docs/e2e-report-2026-02-14.md docs/releases/ scripts/lib/README.md && git commit -m 'docs(i18n): translate top-level README, AGENTS, docs index, extension guide, releases, scripts/lib README to pt-BR'`.
acceptance_criteria: All 9 listed files have a Portuguese-prose diff. README.md headings such as 'Quick Start', 'Why oh-my-kiro?', 'Commands', 'Architecture' are translated (or kept in English where consecrated, but consistently).
Every fenced code block in the touched files is byte-identical to the pre-edit content.
AGENTS.md still contains the literal English strings 'Evidence before claims' (it is a consecrated principle name) AND the original Chinese parentheticals.
`bash tests/test-agents-template.sh 2>&1 | tail -1` shows the same pass/fail counts as baseline.txt.

No em dashes (—) introduced — `grep -n '—' README.md AGENTS.md docs/INDEX.md docs/EXTENSION-GUIDE.md docs/e2e-report-2026-02-14.md docs/releases/v*.md scripts/lib/README.md` returns no matches that were not in the original (compare with `git diff` to confirm).
verification: git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD  # only the listed files

for f in README.md docs/EXTENSION-GUIDE.md docs/releases/v1.2.0.md; do diff <(awk '/^```/{p=1-p; print; next} p' "$f") <(git show HEAD~1:"$f" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^```/{p=1-p; print; next} p') && echo "$f code blocks unchanged" || echo "$f code blocks DIFFER"; done
